days.title: Kernel Tree, Kconfig, Kbuild, and the Context Map

questions.prompt: What do VERSION, PATCHLEVEL, and SUBLEVEL in the top Makefile name?
options: The snapshot of this source tree
The preemption model selected for the running host
The number of CPUs the kernel will boot
questions.explanation: Those three assignments are the tree's version. This week's landmarks were read from 6.12.0, commit adc218676eef. The host that runs the lab may be a different kernel.

questions.prompt: What does kernel/Kconfig.preempt choose?
options: Which IRQ numbers exist on the machine
Which preemption model the build includes
questions.explanation: The choice, including PREEMPT_NONE and PREEMPT_VOLUNTARY, changes which reschedule hooks are compiled. It does not make hardirq context sleepable.

questions.prompt: What does in_task() claim, in the non-PREEMPT_RT form in this tree?
options: The CPU is running a user instruction
preempt_count has no NMI, hardirq, or softirq bits set
The task is allowed to call schedule from a spinlock
A device interrupt is being handled
questions.explanation: in_task() is the complement of the NMI, hardirq, and softirq fields. A syscall runs in task context. That is not the same statement as 'this function may sleep'.

questions.prompt: What does the Day 1 landmark script do with LINUX_SRC?
options: It configures and boots that tree
It reads the pinned v6.12 files and does not modify them
It writes a .config next to the Makefile
It loads a module from that tree
questions.explanation: check-source.sh greps the snapshot and prints source_modified=no. The suite also hashes the kernel Makefile before and after.

questions.prompt: Which function is the live x86-64 syscall dispatch in this 6.12 tree?
options: x64_sys_call, a switch built from the syscall table header
questions.explanation: syscall_64.c says sys_call_table is no longer used for the call. do_syscall_x64 assigns regs->ax from x64_sys_call after array_index_nospec.

questions.prompt: When does entry_SYSCALL_64 take SYSRET?
options: On every return, because it is faster
Only when do_syscall_64 says the user frame is a clean 64-bit return
questions.explanation: SYSRET mishandles non-canonical addresses. A dirty frame, Xen PV, or a bad CS/SS/RIP uses the IRET path instead.

questions.prompt: How does ToyOS enter its teaching syscall?
questions.explanation: arch.c installs syscall_int_stub at vector 128. That is the Week 8 educational gate, not entry_SYSCALL_64.

questions.prompt: What does syscall_lab prove?
options: Which return instruction the kernel used
That getpid and a one-byte pipe write completed in this process
The layout of pt_regs on the kernel stack
questions.explanation: The markers are getpid_matches and pipe_byte. entry_path_claim=none is part of the result.

questions.prompt: What is bit 1 of the x86 page-fault error code in trap_pf.h?
questions.explanation: X86_PF_WRITE is BIT(1). Bit 0 is protection versus not-present. Bit 2 is a user access. Bit 4 is an instruction fetch.

questions.prompt: Linux 0.12 mm/page.s branches on which fact?
options: The present bit of the error code, choosing do_no_page or do_wp_page
Whether the fault came from an MSI
questions.explanation: A clear present bit calls do_no_page. A set bit calls do_wp_page. Both return through iret. The stub does not search an exception table.

questions.prompt: Where does exc_page_fault in this tree get the fault address?
options: Always from a userspace pointer argument
From FRED event data when that feature is on, otherwise from CR2
questions.explanation: The handler line is address = fred_event_data(regs) when X86_FEATURE_FRED is enabled, and read_cr2() otherwise.

questions.prompt: What does the child SIGSEGV in fault_lab show?
options: That the kernel reported the PROT_NONE store to that child as a signal
That the faulting instruction was resumed
questions.explanation: The parent reaps SIGSEGV. irq_claim=none. The lab does not identify the vma or the fixup path.

days.title: Hardware Interrupts, IRQ Descriptors, and Handlers

questions.prompt: Which pointer on irq_desc is the flow handler?
options: handle_irq, which decides mask and ack and then walks actions
questions.explanation: handle_irq is the flow, such as handle_level_irq. The driver's function is irqaction->handler. A shared line chains more than one action.

questions.prompt: What does IRQF_SHARED require of two drivers on one line?
options: Both registrations pass the flag, and each has its own dev_id
They must share one dev_id cookie
questions.explanation: __setup_irq rejects a second action unless both sides set IRQF_SHARED. The cookie is how the right driver is freed later.

questions.prompt: What is /proc/interrupts?
options: The function that runs the driver
A counter and name view, not a handler trace
A file the lab writes to request an IRQ
questions.explanation: The lab prints readable or unreadable and does not assert counts. A comma on a line is a shared name list, not proof you saw the handler run.

questions.prompt: How does a GICv3 end-of-interrupt differ from the 0.12 PIC?
options: gic_eoi_irq writes the hwirq to a system register, not port 0x20
questions.explanation: 0.12 acknowledges the master PIC with an out to port 0x20. gic_eoi_irq in irq-gic-v3.c writes ICC_EOIR1_EL1. The Linux object above both is still irq_desc.

questions.prompt: Which three deferrals does this day keep separate?
questions.explanation: raise_softirq marks a fixed slot. request_threaded_irq wakes irq/N. queue_work_on enqueues work for a worker. The names are not interchangeable.

questions.prompt: Which of these may sleep?
options: A softirq action and a WQ_BH item
A threaded IRQ handler and a normal workqueue worker
The hardirq handler and ksoftirqd's softirq action
questions.explanation: The IRQ thread and worker_thread are process context and may sleep. Softirq context, including WQ_BH and the function ksoftirqd runs, may not.

questions.prompt: What is the eventfd and timerfd lab?
options: A userspace poll analog, labeled as not an IRQ, softirq, or workqueue
questions.explanation: poll reports readiness. The markers not_an_irq_handler, not_a_softirq, and not_a_workqueue forbid reading that as the kernel mechanism.

questions.prompt: Why does this tree ask you not to add softirq slots casually?
options: The enum is a fixed, high-frequency set ending at NR_SOFTIRQS
Softirqs are how every driver must sleep
TASKLET_SOFTIRQ is the only legal slot
questions.explanation: HI through RCU are the slots. The comment above the enum says almost every new job should be a tasklet or another deferral, not a new softirq.

questions.prompt: Why must driver code not use in_atomic() to decide whether it may sleep?
options: It cannot see every spinlock, especially on a non-preemptible kernel
questions.explanation: preempt.h says in_atomic() is preempt_count() != 0 and that it must not be used in drivers as the general sleep test.

questions.prompt: What does might_sleep() do in this tree?
options: It picks the next task the way the Week 15 scheduler will
It warns if the context is atomic, and it may be a voluntary reschedule point
questions.explanation: The macro calls __might_sleep and might_resched. The warning and the preemption point are different jobs. Week 15 owns what a reschedule does with the run queue.

questions.prompt: Which contexts must not sleep?
options: Hardirq, softirq, and a WQ_BH work item
Process context and a normal worker thread
questions.explanation: Hardirq and softirq context must not call schedule. WQ_BH runs in softirq context. A worker thread and ordinary process context may sleep if they hold no forbidding lock.

questions.prompt: What does context_lab's blocking poll demonstrate?
options: That a userspace wait can block, which is not kernel atomic context
Which task Week 15 would run next
questions.explanation: A zero timeout returns immediately. The timerfd wait does not. kernel_preempt_claim=none and scheduler_dive=deferred_to_week_15 are part of the output.

days.title: Entry and Interrupt Tracing and the Debugging Report

questions.prompt: What does seeing trace_irq_handler_entry in handle.c prove?
options: That a tracer ran on this host
That the hook exists in this source snapshot
That tracefs was enabled by the lab
questions.explanation: The call is in the source between the trace pair. The lab does not enable a tracer. A readable tracefs file is still a SKIP.

questions.prompt: What should optional strace, perf, or tracefs print when they cannot be used?
questions.explanation: A missing tool or a blocked ptrace is a skip. Enabling a tracer is out of scope, so tracefs stays a skip even if the file is readable.

questions.prompt: What is voluntary_ctxt_switches in /proc/self/status, for this week?
options: The scheduler's pick of the next task
A field that may be present, not a Week 15 scheduling diagram
questions.explanation: The report prints present or absent. The count is not an explanation of schedule(). That explanation is Week 15.

questions.prompt: What does a passing Day 7 wrapper claim about mastery?
options: Nothing. mastery_claim=none, and the quiz does not grade the report
The learner can write an IRQ handler
The host kernel is the pinned 6.12 commit
questions.explanation: The report records uname and the non-claims. The host release can differ from the source pin. Finishing the wrapper does not complete mastery.
